correctness.rationale: For all real p>1 and q in (0,1), the uniformly convergent reciprocal Hardy products define bounded inverse multipliers. Exact similarity to diagonal C_q proves the complete simple eigenbasis and compact spectrum. Boundary ±1 maximize/minimize the multiplier modulus simultaneously for all factors; analytic Fejér polynomial sequences make both Riesz estimates sharp. Rank-one coefficient duality gives every P_n norm. Improper Riemann sums yield π²/6 and π²/12 and an explicit ε² boundary arc proves Hardy norms have identical exponential rates. CHECK.py finite coefficient tests supplement but do not substitute these infinite arguments.

value.rationale: A natural atomic subfamily of a newly studied integral operator has an intrinsic, exactly normalized spectral recovery problem whose condition number is determined completely for all exponent/atom parameters. Exact every-index spectral projector norms detect nonnormal amplification absent from eigenvalue locations. Sharp exponential boundary-approach rates quantify when such spectral coordinate methods become impractical and distinguish basis vs projector instability; neither follows from boundedness or eigenvalues alone without quantitative Hardy/q-series analysis.
